issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath Normative Release §6.8 Operator precedence (dot/function invocation has higher precedence than unary +/-; explicit example -7.combine(3) is an error)
issues.evidence: FP-02 EXPLORER probe .temp/qa/fp02_explorer_probe.py compared native C++ and forced Python fallback. Expression `-7.combine(3)` on a Patient resource returned native row (["-7"], "-7", "[-7]", NULL, -7.0, true), while forced fallback returned empty/NULL and fhirpath_is_valid=false. The spec's own §6.8 example says `-7.combine(3)` parses as `-(7.combine(3))` and errors because unary negation cannot apply to a list.
issues.root_cause: Native `Evaluator::evalUnaryOp()` evaluated the operand collection and then applied unary +/- to `operand[0]` without checking whether the operand had multiple items. Because the parser correctly binds dot invocation before unary operators, `-7.combine(3)` produced a two-item operand but native silently negated the first item.
issues.resolution: Added a general multi-item singleton guard in native `evalUnaryOp()` before applying unary +/- and rebuilt/copied the bundled DuckDB extension.
issues.verified_in: `.temp/qa/fp02_explorer_probe_final.log` (46 cases, mismatch_count=0); `python3 -m pytest fhir4ds/fhirpath/duckdb/tests/integration/test_operator_parity.py -q` (8 passed); `./build/release/test/unittest '*fhirpath*'` (342 assertions); full conformance `validation_summary.log` (2822/2822)

issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath Normative Release §6.8 Operator precedence (unary + and unary - are valid unary operators below dot/function invocation)
issues.evidence: During focused parity coverage for QA-001, forced Python fallback `fhirpath(?::JSON, '+7.combine(3)')` raised FHIRPathSyntaxError from a wrapper precheck that classifies leading `+` as invalid syntax. The spec lists unary `+` together with unary `-`; `+7.combine(3)` is syntactically valid and should parse as `+(7.combine(3))`, then fail singleton evaluation and return empty/NULL at the public wrapper boundary.
issues.root_cause: The forced Python fallback precheck classified leading `+` as an invalid leading binary operator even though FHIRPath defines unary `+` as a valid unary operator.
issues.resolution: Removed `+` from the fallback wrapper/evaluator leading-binary-operator rejection patterns so unary plus reaches normal parsing/evaluation and public row resilience.
issues.verified_in: `.temp/qa/fp02_explorer_probe_final.log` (46 cases, mismatch_count=0); `python3 -m pytest fhir4ds/fhirpath/duckdb/tests/integration/test_operator_parity.py -q` (8 passed); full conformance `validation_summary.log` (2822/2822)
